card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.
card.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026

card.label: H.R. 7006
card.summary: H.R. 7006 is a consolidated appropriations bill that provides federal funding for fiscal year 2026 for financial services, general government operations, the national security apparatus, the Department of State, foreign operations, and related agencies. It combines two regular appropriations acts: the Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, 2026, and the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026. The legislation establishes funding levels, spending restrictions, administrative mandates, and reporting requirements for numerous federal departments and independent agencies.

summary: This bill provides annual federal appropriations for fiscal year 2026 for the Department of the Treasury, the Executive Office of the President, the judiciary, the District of Columbia, and numerous independent federal agencies. It outlines funding amounts, management requirements, and numerous policy restrictions governing federal programs, personnel, and agency operations.

affected_groups.effect: Receive annual appropriations and must adhere to strict administrative controls, reporting requirements, and spending limitations.
IRS operations, taxpayer services, enforcement activities, and employee training requirements are funded and regulated under specific statutory limits.
affected_groups.group: Internal Revenue Service employees and taxpayers

affected_groups.effect: Local government operations, resident tuition support programs, school improvement programs, and local statutory autonomy are directly affected by federal payments and congressional policy riders.
Eligible for loan programs, entrepreneurial development grants, and business assistance through the Small Business Administration.

key_provisions: Appropriates funds for the Department of the Treasury, including taxpayer services and enforcement at the Internal Revenue Service.
Provides funding for the Executive Office of the President and funds appropriated to the President, including drug control and high-intensity drug trafficking area programs.
Allocates funds for the federal judiciary, covering the Supreme Court, courts of appeals, district courts, defender services, and court security.
Provides federal payments and local fund approvals for the District of Columbia, covering resident tuition support, courts, public defender services, and school improvement programs.

Funds various independent agencies such as the Consumer Product Safety Commission, Federal Communications Commission, Federal Trade Commission, General Services Administration, National Archives and Records Administration, Office of Personnel Management, Securities and Exchange Commission, and Small Business Administration.
Sets wide-ranging general provisions and restrictions for executive branch agencies, including prohibitions on funding certain types of training, public relations, and specific agency rules.
Imposes restrictions on District of Columbia local laws and spending, including rules concerning assisted suicide, abortion, and vehicle emissions standards.
